newsitem.title: PERU: Peru cenbank reserve requirements costly to banks.
newsitem.headline: Peru cenbank reserve requirements costly to banks.

text.p: Reserve requirements imposed by the Central Reserve Bank are driving up the cost of money for Peruvian banks, driving them to go abroad to finance transactions, analysts said.

"The percentage reserve requirement, especially for dollars, is very high, generating ill effects for banks, which is why they try to avoid them," said Jorge Chavez, head of Maximice consulting firm and a former central bank president.

The central bank retains in reserve $0.45 for each dollar and nine centimos for each sol deposited in the 23 banks operating in the country, arguing the requirement allows it to control liquidity in Peru's financial system.
Analysts say the system is flawed.

"It is proven the world over that the reserve requirement is not an adequate instrument in modern economies," Chavez said. "The central bank should eliminate it or, in any case, reduce it or work with other market mechanisms."
Banks today avoid the requirement by making deposits abroad that later return as loans, he said.
Giorgio Bernasconi, treasury unit manager of Banco Continental, said that at present "it is more profitable to take foreign loans than seek deposits from the public."
He said reduced reserve requirements would shrink the gap between the two options.
